vexillum, vexillī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

flag, banner

Classically the army’s cloth banner, a diminutive of vēlum (Lewis & Short; de Vaan 660). Traupman uses it for a national flag (p. 27) and gives vexillum quassāre, to wave a flag (p. 404).

Examples

  • Vexillum ventō agitātur.

    The flag is flapping in the wind.composed

  • signō indicāre

    to flagTraupman 316

  • vexillum quassāre

    to wave a flagTraupman 404

SourcesLewis & Short: vexillum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 27, 316, 404. Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 660, s.v. vēlum. Morgan–Owens has only the royal standard, vexillum rēgāle; Levi–Bini has no entry.: p. 316.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
